observable_outcome: Every registered Wiki note is atomic, source-linked, deep, detailed, example-backed and contains a domain-appropriate implementation artifact plus a Mermaid mechanism diagram.

acceptance_checks.stable_identity: note_id, primary_question, note_type and status on every note
acceptance_checks.lineage: source_ids, Reference and Source coverage on every note
acceptance_checks.atomicity: one primary question and one primary concept per note; no multi-concept title finding
acceptance_checks.depth: at least 1700 words and required explanatory sections
acceptance_checks.example: a bounded worked example with input, decision and observable outcome
acceptance_checks.code: a fenced domain-appropriate executable example, contract or pseudocode artifact
acceptance_checks.diagram: a valid Mermaid block tied to the note concept
acceptance_checks.mirror_parity: every reference_path artifact and its Wiki mirror are byte-identical
acceptance_checks.global_regression: formatter, source coverage, relationship and retrieval checks pass

non_goals: Changing immutable source PDFs or source facts
Claiming learner mastery or production validation
stop_conditions: A note cannot be mapped to its registered source or reference artifact
A generated artifact would misrepresent a source claim
A mandatory global validator fails after remediation
